purpose: Adapters for the first strict nineteenth-century survey batch. Every 07K entry has an explicit 1800-1899 object, maker, collection, trade, use, or provenance node.
guards: Current museum infrastructure may be modern; the harvested historical object or batch must retain its explicit nineteenth-century date/provenance anchor.
Preserve later museum acquisition, donation, sale and rediscovery as separate custody events rather than replacing the nineteenth-century object date.
Do not collapse maker, preparer, seller, owner/collector, donor and current holder into one relation.
Use JSON or IIIF metadata where advertised, but do not fetch image binaries in the census workflow.

adapters.promotion_rule: Capture parent case/set, child records, object number, maker/preparer, made date and current collection separately; follow advertised JSON/IIIF metadata only.

adapters.institution_scope: OHSU Historical Collections & Archives digital collections
adapters.target: Medical Museum Collection microscope-slide case records
adapters.promotion_rule: Keep object date, later donor/date, box number, chest structure, label state and IIIF manifest as distinct fields.

adapters.institution_scope: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
adapters.promotion_rule: Capture inscription-based attribution, accession/catalogue IDs, physical box/set structure and related maker/place/date fields without upgrading probable attribution to certainty.

adapters.institution_scope: Whipple Museum of the History of Science
adapters.target: historical microscope-slide cases and individually significant labelled slides
adapters.promotion_rule: Capture accession number, bounded date range, maker/seller labels, case/tray structure, damage/broken-slide notes and museum purchase provenance.
Preserve the household cabinet provenance, successive-generation use, individual handwritten labels and modern discovery/custody as separate events.
